title: Spider Bite: Zoe Stuns Alan by 1.74 as Sonny's 146.72 Crashes the Title Race
dek: A 28% underdog snapped Team Pillbert's five-game streak, The Horse is Hea posted the week's top score, and the HULK won by 37 and somehow lost ground in the title odds.
body: Ghostu-Spider SZN entered Week 7 as a 28% underdog against a Team Pillbert side that hadn't lost since Week 1, and walked off with an 87.96 to 86.22 win. Neither team's receivers wanted any part of it: Nico Collins scored 1.6 for Zoe on a 14.01 projection, and Jalen Coker answered with 1.4 for Alan on a 12.57 projection, a 0.2-point duel of disappointment. Javonte Williams did his job for Team Pillbert with 21.5, but Justin Jefferson's 6.4 and Chuba Hubbard's 8 left Alan 1.74 points short. Z² snapped a two-game skid, moved to 3-4, and became the first person since the opener to beat Team Pillbert.

The upset rearranged the board more for the loser than the winner. Team Pillbert is still 5-2 with 94% playoff odds, but its title odds fell from 26% to 17%, and it slid from second to third. Zoe's win kept her alive rather than launching her: Ghostu-Spider SZN's 660.4 points are the fewest among the three 3-4 teams, and her playoff odds sit at 6%. She also swapped David Montgomery for Blake Corum, and the rookie now gets a week to prove the upset was a turning point and not a one-off.

The week's loudest scoreboard belonged to Sonny. The Horse is Hea dropped 146.72 on Randy's The fumblers in a 38.2-point road win, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.8), Jameson Williams (23.6 on an 8.95 projection) and Bucky Irving (23.5 on a 12.81 projection) all landing among the week's six best performances. George Pickens (13.7) and Ollie Gordon II (16.8) both started and both delivered, which is a sentence nobody expected to write after last week. The Horse is Hea is 5-2 in second place, and its title odds leapt from 11% to 28%, the biggest jump in the league.

Randy's slide has hit four games. Caleb Williams gave him 22.12 on a 17.59 projection, but Derrick Henry posted 5.4 on a 17.37 projection, his second straight week under six points while projected above 17. The fumblers are 3-4 with 752.4 points, still fifth, but their playoff odds are down to 24% and their title odds are 3%. The good news is that Randy clearly isn't standing still, as the transaction log will show.

The coin flip of the week went decisively to Kaushal. Habibsters won 119.84 to 93.58 at Dawgs, a 50-50 pregame matchup, behind Drake Maye's 27.44 on a 20.59 projection. The strange part: Tony Pollard scored 35 on Habibi's bench, the biggest bench blunder of the week by more than 11 points, and it didn't matter because the margin was 26.26. Mekhi had his own bench pain with Tee Higgins' 23.8 sitting while Ashton Jeanty started for 17.6, and Dawgs fell to 2-5 with 9% playoff odds. Habibsters, meanwhile, are 3-4 on a two-game win streak, sit fourth, and saw their title odds climb from 6% to 15%.

Ramon's No Banner only HULK beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 98 to 60.88 as an 85% favorite, leaving Zay Flowers' 23.7 on the bench and still winning by 37.12. Jordan had the best individual performance in the entire league, Joe Burrow's 28.88 on a 19.31 projection, and the rest of the lineup combined for exactly 32 points. The HULK is 6-1 with 927.4 points and 100% playoff odds, yet its title odds dropped from 50% to 37%, the second straight week a comfortable win came with a lower number. Jordan is 1-6 with 0% playoff odds, and swapped Ladd McConkey for J.K. Dobbins on the way out of the week.

The transaction log was a two-man show. Sonny made seven moves, the busiest commissioner in the business: Lamar Jackson in for Patrick Mahomes (yes, the same Lamar that Zoe cut last week), C.J. Stroud for Bryce Young, Jordan Mason for Cam Skattebo, Will Reichard for Terry McLaurin, Broncos D/ST for 49ers D/ST, and Emanuel Wilson in and back out for Zach Charbonnet. Randy matched him with ten entries, cutting Kenny Gainwell, Alec Pierce, Darren Waller, Jordan Addison and the Rams D/ST while adding Jaylin Noel, DeMario Douglas, Cameron Dicker, the Browns D/ST and the Bears D/ST. Ramon picked up Brandon Aubrey, the kicker Randy cut a week ago, Mekhi added Aaron Rodgers, and Kaushal brought in Germie Bernard and Tre Tucker. The title picture now reads HULK 37%, The Horse is Hea 28%, Team Pillbert 17%, Habibsters 15%, and nobody else above 3%.

Week 8 has a headliner: Team Pillbert vs The Horse is Hea, two 5-2 teams that traded Hubbard and Smith for Pickens and Gordon two weeks ago and now get to settle it on the field. Habibsters face Ghostu-Spider SZN, where Kaushal can tighten his grip on fourth and Zoe can prove the Alan win wasn't a fluke. Randy hosts Jordan with a four-game skid on the line against the league's 1-6 team, a game The fumblers simply cannot lose. And the HULK takes on Dawgs, where Kai needs a miracle and the league leader needs to stop winning in ways the model finds unconvincing.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider SZN Fan Club
social.text: 28% they said. 87.96 to 86.22. Nico Collins gave us 1.6 points and we STILL ended a five-game streak. Imagine what happens when he shows up.

social.author: Dale Prognosticator
social.text: Team Pillbert's five-game streak ends by 1.74 with Jalen Coker at 1.4 on a 12.57 projection. Streaks don't die in blowouts. They die in decimals.

social.author: The Horse is Hea Hive
social.text: 146.72. JSN 26.8, Jameson 23.6, Bucky 23.5. Pickens and Gordon started and put up 30.5. Title odds 11% to 28%. Remember when that trade was a disaster? Team Pillbert next. Bring Hubbard.

social.author: Buckaroo Insider
social.text: Sources: Habibsters left Tony Pollard's 35 points on the bench and won by 26.26 anyway. Sources say the lineup is under review, strictly for style points.

social.author: GV Sideline Society
social.text: Joe Burrow: 28.88, the best score by any player in the league this week. Everyone else in our lineup: 32 combined. Joe deserves teammates.

social.author: Fumblers Faithful
social.text: Caleb 22.12. Henry 5.4. Four straight losses. Five guys cut, Bears D/ST added. If we're going down, the defense will at least be wearing navy and orange.

social.author: HULK Smash Club
social.text: Won by 37.12. Zay Flowers 23.7 on the bench. 6-1, 927.4 points. Title odds went DOWN to 37%. The model is scared of something, and it isn't the scoreboard.

social.author: Dawg Pound BFL
social.text: Higgins 23.8 on the bench, Jeanty 17.6 in the lineup. 2-5, 9% playoff odds, Aaron Rodgers added. HULK next. Long shots are still shots.

social.author: Waiver Wire Watch
social.text: Lamar Jackson: cut by Ghostu-Spider SZN last week, scooped by The Horse is Hea this week. Spider SZN still beat Team Pillbert without him. Everybody's happy except Mahomes's old roster spot.

trade_watch.take: The comeback week Sonny needed: Pickens (13.7) and Gordon (16.8) both started for 30.5, while Hubbard managed 8 and Smith didn't play a role. Alan still leads 43.6 to 30.5 in lineup points, but a 35.6-point gap is now 13.1, and the two sides meet head to head next week.

Javonte Williams put up 21.5 for Alan and is now at 75.5 since the deal, every point of it in Team Pillbert's lineup. Diggs sat with zero and is stuck on 6 lineup points for Randy, so the winner just keeps pulling away, even in a week Alan lost.
Jeanty's 17.6 pushes Mekhi's haul to 65.6 points since the trade, with Adams adding 25. Jefferson's 6.4 leaves Alan at 22.2, so this one is still clearly Kai's, even if his record doesn't show it.

Jordan still owns the scoreboard here, 56.2 lineup points to Alan's zero, since Jeanty went straight to Dawgs. But Likely (2.2) and Boston (4.2) gave him just 6.4 this week, and Egbuka still has zero lineup points for Jordan, which is a lot of trade return spending time on the bench.

bios.1: Sonny's team scored a league-best 146.72 in Week 7 and leapt from 11% to 28% in title odds, the biggest jump of the week. At 5-2 with 98% playoff odds and a freshly churned roster that now includes Lamar Jackson, it's the hottest contender in the room. Next week's rematch with trade partner Team Pillbert could decide second place.
bios.2: Randy has lost four straight and sits at 3-4 with 24% playoff odds, despite Caleb Williams' 22.12 in Week 7. Derrick Henry has been the anchor in the wrong sense, and Randy responded with ten roster moves in one week. A home game against 1-6 Counting or not Counting GV is about as must-win as it gets.
bios.3: Jordan is 1-6 with 0% playoff odds after a 60.88-point outing that featured the week's best individual performance, Joe Burrow's 28.88. The supporting cast is the problem, and J.K. Dobbins replacing Ladd McConkey is the latest attempt to fix it. A matchup with slumping The fumblers is the best chance at a spoiler win in a while.
bios.4: Alan's five-game win streak ended by 1.74 points to a 28% underdog, and the title odds slid from 26% to 17%. At 5-2 with 94% playoff odds, the season is far from in trouble, but the receivers need to wake up after Coker's 1.4 and Jefferson's 6.4. Next up is Sonny and the trade both of them want to win.
bios.5: Mekhi is 2-5 after a 26-point loss to Habibsters, with Tee Higgins' 23.8 stuck on the bench. The 736 points scored are more than two teams above him, which explains why his 9% playoff odds beat Zoe's. Aaron Rodgers joins the roster just in time for a date with the league-leading HULK.
bios.6: Kaushal is 3-4 but riding a two-game win streak, sitting in the fourth playoff spot with 69% odds and title odds up from 6% to 15%. Drake Maye has become a weekly weapon, and the team won by 26 with Tony Pollard's 35 on the bench. Ghostu-Spider SZN is next in a game that could cement fourth place.
bios.7: Ramon's team is 6-1 with 927.4 points, the most in the league by nearly 74, and its playoff spot is a lock. The only thing it can't seem to beat is the model, which has trimmed its title odds from 55% to 37% over two straight wins. Dawgs are next, and the HULK would like a win the computer actually respects.
bios.8: Zoe pulled off the upset of the week, beating Team Pillbert as a 28% underdog to reach 3-4. The points total of 660.4 keeps her playoff odds at 6%, so the rookie needs to keep stacking wins. Habibsters are next, with fourth place close enough to see.
